description: The last approval, and the one that unlocks everything downstream. The Campus Director signs a second time; the request becomes APPROVED, a CSM record is created for the requestor, and the signatures on the PDF become visible. Rejecting here stops a request that has already passed every other desk.

Stamps the signature, sets finalDirectorStatus APPROVED (which is what the PDF checks), masterStatus APPROVED, completionStatus CSM_PENDING, requestEndAt if null, creates the Csm row and writes the audit log — one transaction, all or nothing.

trpc_procedures.description: Sets finalDirectorStatus and masterStatus to FINAL_REJECTED. No Csm row is created and no signature is required.

functional: finalDirectorStatus === 'APPROVED' is the master gate for the PDF's signatures. Nothing else unlocks them, and no other procedure may set that value.
The approval writes six things plus the Csm row plus the audit log, and every one of them is in the same transaction.
The Csm row is created here, empty, with submittedAt null. The requestor completes it (spec 015).
completionStatus CSM_PENDING is what the requestor's banner and their CSM route both key on.
requestEndAt is set only if it was null, so a retry cannot move the completion date.
Approving requires a signature; the URL is copied onto the request.
Rejecting requires a note, requires no signature, and creates no Csm row.
FINAL_REJECTED is labelled 'Director Final Rejected' everywhere, distinct from the chairperson's 'IDO Final Rejected'.
After approval the page opens read-only with a link to the finished PDF.
authorization: Server gate: roleProcedure('DIRECTOR'), then assertPermission(APPROVE_DIRECTOR), then the stage check on finalDirectorStatus, then the signature check on approval.
The stage check reads finalDirectorStatus. This is the only column that distinguishes the Director's final approval from their first one — both are the same role on the same request.
An IDO_CHAIRPERSON calling finalDirectorApprove gets FORBIDDEN, even though they signed the request moments before.
Nothing about this stage is reachable by a requestor.
ux: The signature summary is the centre of the page. A director countersigning three other signatures must be able to see all three.
The confirmation dialog names all three consequences: approved, signed form released, feedback requested. This is the least reversible action in the system.
A missing signature is explained with a link to the profile before an attempt is made.
After approval the page states plainly that the request is complete and offers the PDF, rather than showing a dead action panel.
Reject is visually secondary and always asks for a reason.

edge_cases: This is the single most consequential write in the app: six columns, a new row in another table and an audit log. Anything less than one transaction can leave an approved request with no CSM, or a CSM with no approval.

Csm.requestId is unique, so a retry after a partial commit throws — which is the correct outcome, because it means the first attempt already succeeded. Surface it as 'already approved', not as a server error.
The PDF gate is finalDirectorStatus === 'APPROVED', not masterStatus. Both are set here, but a future change that sets one without the other silently releases or withholds the signatures.
requestEndAt guarded on null matters for the same reason requestStartAt is: it is the duration the office reports on.
The Director appears twice in the workflow. Routing (spec 009) and both stage guards key on different columns; conflating them lets a director approve the final stage from the first-stage page.
The signature summary reads the request's stored URLs, not the users' current profiles — a signature changed afterwards must not alter what was countersigned.
out_of_scope: The CSM form itself — spec 015; this stage only creates the empty record.
The PDF rendering — spec 016; this stage only flips the gate.
Any post-approval amendment — an approved request is final; there is no reopen.
